prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one high-fidelity desktop web app lesson-player screen, landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge, crisp readable English UI, no device mockup or outer caption. This is a design proposal, not implementation. Product: HISTORY, an interactive history learning app. Same sample chapter in every alternative: The Silk Roads / At the crossroads, chapter 2 of 5. The attached reference contributes ONLY the Worlds identity: inky navy, rich plum, warm ivory, restrained amber controls, classical editorial lettering, luminous historical illustrations. Do not copy its three-phone layout or reuse its art as wallpaper. Preserve compact navigation: HISTORY, Chapters, bookmark, Sources, sound. Bottom controls: Previous, a five-part chapter progress indicator, Next. Narration is optional and user-paced: show Read / Listen, play/pause and seek; Next remains usable while audio plays. Visible prose must teach real history, not give instructions about the UI. No quiz, radio choices, scores, fake citations, generic card dashboard, oversized slogan, giant empty header, or essay hidden below the viewport. Generated historical imagery is visibly labeled Reconstruction; map routes schematic. Composition: a digital illustrated history book designed for reading, NOT a fake 3D book or an app dashboard. A single editorial spread fills the viewport beneath compact chrome. The left half is a beautiful dark-ink reading page with title “The journey changed hands”, a small progress label “Passage 2 of 4”, and three substantial highly legible paragraphs: “The name Silk Roads suggests a continuous journey across a continent. Most trade worked through shorter connections: a merchant might know one region well, sell to another trader, and never see the final destination.” “Cities made those connections possible. In and around Samarkand, people could find markets, storage, transport and contacts. Translation mattered because exchange involved unfamiliar languages and customs as well as prices.” “Goods were only part of what moved. Travellers carried techniques, stories and beliefs, while local communities selected and reshaped what they encountered. A network connected places without making them identical.” A source affordance sits just beneath the prose, “Where this account comes from”. The right half is a newly composed painterly narrative sequence blended into one large luminous illustration: a caravan reaching a city gate, then merchants exchanging a wrapped load in a shaded arcade; subtle small textual annotations point to one transaction, not gamified hotspots. Art is subordinate to the explanation yet spectacular. A narrow four-image passage filmstrip along the bottom shows different art for Arrival / Exchange / Translation / Departure. “Turn to the next passage” is the main action; Read/Listen retains place and optional narration. Text and image change together each passage, never a long article underneath a static background.
purpose: Lesson-player composition proposal; illustrative artwork and unverified generated map/chronology labels.
approval: User 2026-11-22: likes all four, including spatial exploration; build a fluid system using these references.
